description: Cr carbides precipitate at grain boundaries when held ≈450–850 °C, depleting adjacent Cr
typicalNumbers: Risk rises with carbon and exposure time
mitigation: Use L or stabilised (321/347) grades; solution anneal after welding if needed
relevantStandard: ASTM A262 (verify practice letter for service)

description: Tensile stress + chlorides + temperature causes cracking; pitting ranks by PREN
typicalNumbers: Austenitic SCC concern generally above ≈50–60 °C in chlorides
mitigation: Choose duplex/super-duplex/Ni alloys/Ti; reduce stress; coatings

description: Intermetallic σ (≈600–1000 °C) and α′ (≈400–540 °C) cause toughness loss
typicalNumbers: Duplex service limit commonly ≈250–300 °C
mitigation: Respect temperature limits; control weld heat input; solution anneal

materialsAffected: Carbon/low-alloy steels, ferritic SS, Mo, W
description: BCC metals lose toughness at low temperature/high strain rate; FCC (Al, Cu, austenitic, Ni) do not
typicalNumbers: Transition temperature depends on grain size, composition, thickness
mitigation: Specify impact test temperature; use fine-grain/Ni steels or FCC alloys for cold service

materialsAffected: High-strength steels, 17-4 PH H900, Ti, some Ni alloys
description: Atomic H from plating/pickling/cathodic protection causes delayed brittle fracture
typicalNumbers: Susceptibility rises above ≈1000–1200 MPa (≈ >32–35 HRC)
mitigation: Baking after plating (e.g. ≈190–220 °C for hours per ASTM B850, verify); limit hardness

description: Tempering ≈250–400 °C (TME) or slow-cooling through ≈375–575 °C (temper embrittlement from P, Sn, Sb, As) reduces toughness
typicalNumbers: Mo additions reduce susceptibility
mitigation: Avoid embrittling temper ranges; cleaner steel; rapid cooling after temper

description: Hard HAZ + hydrogen + residual stress → cracking
typicalNumbers: IIW CE > ≈0.4 raises preheat need (thickness & process dependent)
mitigation: Preheat, low-hydrogen consumables, PWHT, interpass control

description: Precipitates dissolve/coarsen in HAZ; T6 strength can fall by >40% locally
typicalNumbers: Design codes apply HAZ reduction factors
mitigation: Design for HAZ strength; post-weld ageing where possible; choose 5xxx for welded structures

description: SCC in short-transverse grain direction; exfoliation
typicalNumbers: T73/T76 overaged tempers resist SCC with strength penalty
mitigation: Avoid sustained tensile stress in ST direction; select T73

description: Dissimilar metals in electrolyte; carbon fibre is strongly cathodic to Al/Mg/steel
typicalNumbers: Area ratio (large cathode/small anode) is worst
mitigation: Isolate (sealants/insulating layers), coatings, compatible pairs

description: Gray: low tensile, high compressive (≈3–4× tensile), high damping, notch-insensitive; ductile: notch-sensitive tougher
typicalNumbers: Compressive/tensile ratio approximate
mitigation: Use ductile iron where shock/tension matter; check section-size effects

materialsAffected: Al castings, Mg die-cast, Zn die-cast, iron castings
description: Pores/oxides act as crack initiators; fatigue life tracks largest defect
typicalNumbers: Test bars ≠ casting properties
mitigation: HIP, vacuum/low-pressure casting, X-ray/CT acceptance levels

materialsAffected: Bearing steels, gear steels, spring steels
description: Oxide/sulphide inclusions initiate rolling-contact/high-cycle fatigue
typicalNumbers: Vacuum degassing/VAR/ESR improve cleanliness
mitigation: Specify cleanliness rating & melt route

description: Fine grain increases yield (Hall–Petch) and toughness; abnormal grain growth after critical strain anneal or overheating
typicalNumbers: Coarse grain in Al after small cold work + anneal
mitigation: Control normalising/anneal; add grain-refining elements (Al, Nb, Ti, V)

materialsAffected: Rolled sheet/plate, Mg, Ti, extrusions, CFRP, AM
description: Properties differ by direction (L/LT/ST); earing in deep-drawing
typicalNumbers: CFRP E1 ≫ E2
mitigation: State test direction; use ST data for thick-section design
relevantStandard: ASTM E8 specimen orientation notes; plate L-T/T-L

materialsAffected: Tool steels, alloy steels, carburised parts
description: Non-uniform cooling/phase changes cause warpage and cracks
typicalNumbers: Air-hardening grades (A2, D2) distort less than water-hardening
mitigation: Select quench media/steel grade; stress-relieve before hardening; allow grinding stock

description: Carburising ≈880–950 °C; gas nitriding ≈500–550 °C; induction hardening; anodising; hard chrome; PVD/DLC; shot peening improves fatigue
typicalNumbers: Process temps approximate
mitigation: Specify process, case depth and hardness; control distortion and hydrogen

description: Residual tension lowers fatigue/SCC resistance, causes distortion after machining
typicalNumbers: Magnitude can approach yield in welds/AM
mitigation: Stress relief, peening, balanced machining

description: Free-machining C36000 is the 100% reference for copper alloys; AISI 1212 = 100% for steels; Ti/Ni/Inconel machine slowly with tool wear
typicalNumbers: Ratings are relative, shop-dependent
mitigation: Select grade for process; use coolant/carbide tooling

description: Adhesive wear/seizure between similar metals
mitigation: Dissimilar couples, hard coatings, lubrication

description: Time-dependent strain at ≳0.4 Tm; rupture life by Larson–Miller
typicalNumbers: Polymers creep at RT; Zn creeps at RT
mitigation: Use creep-rupture data; lower stress; larger sections

materialsAffected: Mo, W, Ti, graphite, 310S, Ni alloys
description: Mo forms volatile MoO3 in air above ≈500–600 °C; graphite oxidises >≈400–500 °C
typicalNumbers: Approximate thresholds
mitigation: Inert/vacuum atmosphere or coatings

description: Fines and chips can ignite; Mg fires need Class D extinguishers
mitigation: Dust/chip control, coolant selection, safe storage

description: Dust/fume inhalation → chronic beryllium disease; machining controls required
typicalNumbers: Regulatory exposure limits apply (jurisdiction-specific)
mitigation: Local exhaust, wet machining, regulated handling

description: Pb restricted in some drinking-water/RoHS/REACH contexts
typicalNumbers: Jurisdiction-specific
mitigation: Lead-free alternatives; supplier declarations

description: Alpha case, oxygen/hydrogen pickup, galling, low thermal conductivity machining heat
mitigation: Vacuum/inert heat treatment; remove alpha case; sharp tooling
relevantStandard: ASTM B265/F136; ASTM E1409/E1447 (O, H analysis, verify)

description: Af temperature/superelastic window sets function; fatigue under strain amplitude; welding difficult
typicalNumbers: Af shifts by tens °C for ≈1 at% Ni change
mitigation: Specify Af; DSC and bend-free-recovery tests

description: Moisture lowers PA stiffness/strength and changes dimensions; creep under constant load; UV degrades PC/ABS/PE
typicalNumbers: PA66 saturation moisture several % — datasheet dependent
mitigation: Use conditioned data (e.g. 50% RH), reinforcement, design for creep

description: Strength is statistical (Weibull); contact stress and thermal shock govern failures; compression ≫ tension
typicalNumbers: Weibull modulus m typically ≈5–15 for engineering ceramics
mitigation: Design for compression, avoid stress concentrators, proof test

description: Delamination and barely visible impact damage reduce compression strength; moisture lowers matrix-dominated properties
mitigation: Damage-tolerance design, NDT (UT/thermography), conditioning tests

description: Build orientation anisotropy, porosity, rough surface, powder reuse (O/N pickup), residual stress
mitigation: Stress relief, HIP, machining critical surfaces, lot/powder traceability

description: EN 10204 3.1/3.2 MTC gives chemistry/mechanical results; mislabelled stainless is a known risk; magnet test cannot separate 201/304/316
mitigation: Verify MTC vs heat number; PMI (XRF/OES); independent lab tests for critical parts

description: IS, ASTM, EN, ISO, JIS, GB grades are NOT equivalent unless the standards state it; chemistry, tolerances, test requirements differ
mitigation: Name the exact standard/edition/grade/condition on the PO

materialsAffected: Ni, Co, Mo, Ti alloys; Al; steels
description: Alloy-element price volatility (Ni, Co, Mo) drives cost; recycled Al uses a small fraction of primary-Al energy (commonly cited ≈5%); steel EAF vs BF route changes embodied CO2
typicalNumbers: Not verified numerically here
mitigation: Get live quotes; check recycled content/EPDs; dual-source grades

materialsAffected: Ti alloys, Ni superalloys, Be, composites
description: Some alloys/forms are export-controlled or require end-use declarations
typicalNumbers: Jurisdiction-specific
mitigation: Check regulations before export/import
